output.summary: A herbaceous annual or short-lived perennial native to North America and East Asia, upright yellow woodsorrel has three heart-shaped leaflets that close at night. Its ripe capsules burst when disturbed, scattering seeds. All parts are edible and tangy, but only small quantities should be eaten because oxalic acid can hinder calcium absorption; the root is excluded when eaten raw.
output.edibilityNote: All parts are edible, but only in small quantities; leaves, flowers and green pods may be eaten raw, while the root is excluded from raw use.
